idea.heading: The Idea
idea.body: Terra explores how porous ceramics and water can create a simple, passive cooling system for urban spaces. Rainwater is absorbed by the ceramic elements and slowly released through evaporation, cooling the surrounding air while the structure provides shade.

result.heading: The Result
result.bodyBlack: A modular urban cooling spot that combines shade, evaporative cooling and water to create a more comfortable microclimate. Individual ceramic elements can be replaced, allowing the system to adapt, be maintained and evolve over time.

problem.heading: The Problem
problem.body: Cities are increasingly affected by heat, while sealed surfaces and a lack of vegetation intensify local heat build-up. Public spaces often provide little protection from direct sunlight and high temperatures.
